items.title: How long does the dedupe window need to last to actually stop duplicates?
items.description: A message can be redelivered any time up until the queue's visibility timeout expires — L2's payment worker uses a 5-minute (300s) timeout. Drag how long the consumer's dedupe key is kept before it expires, and see how many of a batch of 1,000 redelivered messages still slip through as duplicate charges once the dedupe key has already expired and been forgotten.
items.compute: const visibilityTimeoutSeconds = 300; const batchSize = 1000; const uncoveredFraction = Math.max(0, (visibilityTimeoutSeconds - params.dedupeTtlSeconds) / visibilityTimeoutSeconds); const duplicateChargesSlippedThrough = Math.round(batchSize * uncoveredFraction * 0.2); return { duplicateChargesSlippedThrough };

items.title: What happens to queue depth when producers outrun consumers?
items.description: The payment worker processes messages at a fixed rate. Drag how fast the producer (checkout) writes new messages per second, and see where queue depth settles after 5 minutes if consumer throughput can't keep up.
items.compute: const consumerRatePerSecond = 20; const durationSeconds = 300; const netRate = params.producerRatePerSecond - consumerRatePerSecond; const queueDepthAfter5Min = Math.max(0, Math.round(netRate * durationSeconds)); return { queueDepthAfter5Min };
